country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title; PDF p. 2, Introducción

effect_estimate.comment: Historical-institutional narrative accompanied only by descriptive 2010 Census coverage percentages and a public spending series (1993-2009); no econometric or inferential statistical effect estimate is estimated.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Historical-institutional analysis shows that successive cycles of decentralization (1979-1983), partial re-provincialization (1985-1987), privatization (1999-2006), and re-statization (2002-2006) consolidated three fragmented provision subsystems (national, provincial, and local) with weak intergovernmental coordination, parallel regulatory/planning agencies, and persistent territorial inequality. Descriptive 2010 Census figures show overall network coverage of 75.47% of dwellings (75.09% of households; 3,596,587 households) for piped water and 48.65% of dwellings (47.57% of households; 2,278,609 households) for sewerage: 74.56% water and 41.83% sewerage in the national subsystem (AySA, 17 municipalities, 47.9% of households), 69.6% water and 41.8% sewerage in the provincial subsystem (ABSA, 51 municipalities, 32.56% of households, with acute deficits in outer Conurbano districts such as Malvinas Argentinas at 10.26% water / 2.08% sewerage and José C. Paz at 17.29% / 5.95%), and 80.94% water and 52.07% sewerage in the local subsystem (66 municipalities, 19.54% of households).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Resumen/Abstract; PDF pp. 12-13, De regreso al Estado, Gráficos 2-4; PDF pp. 16-17, Conclusiones

mechanism_certainty.comment: Ceiling for historical-institutional / qualitative studies is 2. Primary normative, regulatory, and judicial mechanisms (statutory/decree service-area transfers, residential disconnection rules and 1984 cutoff ban, Law 10.474 50% low-income tariff exemption, concession rescission under Decree 1666/06 for missed coverage targets, Supreme Court enforcement of <= 0.01 mg/L arsenic limits and Matanza-Riachuelo municipal coverage mandates, and parallel uncoordinated regulatory/planning bodies) are directly documented from laws, decrees, institutional records, and court rulings.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 4-17, La institucionalización y trayectoria de los servicios & Los intentos de coordinación; PDF p. 18, Normativas

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines multi-level institutional fragmentation across three subsystems and failed provincial coordination/master-planning efforts (OSBA, ORAB, OCABA, DIPAC, 1989/1995/2011 plans), jurisdictional service-area transfers and concession boundaries, tariff/connection-fee regimes, Law 10.474 Art. 22 50% hardship tariff exemption for low-income households, 1976 residential disconnection/lien rules and 1984 prohibition of total disconnection for non-payment, regulatory fines/sanctions and contract rescission, user complaints and Supreme Court judicial review (Matanza-Riachuelo and 9 de Julio arsenic amparo rulings), and union (SOSBA) / user-association participation.
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, ENFORCEMENT, institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination, planning, service_area, fees, hardship_exception, disconnection, sanction, judicial_review, complaint, participation
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 4-15, La institucionalización y trayectoria de los servicios & Los intentos de coordinación; PDF pp. 16-17, Conclusiones

outcome_flags.comment: Analyzes network water and sewerage coverage and access modalities (piped public network vs wells/pumps and septic tanks/cesspits), mandatory/actual household formal connection, water quality (2000 Bahía Blanca algae crisis; 9 de Julio arsenic levels), service continuity/interruptions and disconnections, and tariff affordability/hardship relief.
outcome_flags.value: service_coverage, water_access, sanitation_access, formal_connection, service_quality, service_continuity, affordability
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 2, Introducción; PDF p. 4, Orígenes; PDF pp. 6, 8-13, Gráficos 2-4; PDF pp. 14-17

publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, journal header and article history footer

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Although the author describes the overarching approach as a qualitative narrative case study consulting institutional reports, laws, census data, and key informant interviews, the article itself operationalizes a 1973-2012 historical-institutional and legal-regulatory analysis of provincial/national statutes, decrees, concession contracts, regulatory bodies, Supreme Court decisions, and descriptive macro census/expenditure statistics, with no primary participant interview sample or interview data reported, matching the Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework for historical-institutional studies.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 1, Resumen/Abstract; PDF pp. 2-3, Introducción; PDF p. 18, Normativas

sample_size.comment: Single-jurisdiction case study of the Province of Buenos Aires (15,625,084 inhabitants in 2010 across 24 Greater Buenos Aires partidos and 111 interior partidos; 2010 Census coverage reported across 3 subsystems covering 51 provincial, 17 national, and 66 local municipalities, totaling 3,596,587 households with piped water and 2,278,609 with sewerage). Exact numbers of key informant interviews and documentary sources consulted are not reported in the paper.
sample_size.value: 1 province case study (Province of Buenos Aires, encompassing 3 provision subsystems across 134–135 municipalities/partidos; exact number of key informant interviews and documentary sources not reported)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 2-3, Introducción; PDF p. 12, De regreso al Estado

study_design.comment: Described by the author as a qualitative methodology with a narrative approach taking the Province of Buenos Aires (1973-2012, with historical background from 1882) as a case study, drawing on institutional reports, provincial and national laws/decrees, population census data, and key informant interviews.
study_design.value: Qualitative historical-institutional case study with narrative approach (documentary and legal/normative analysis, descriptive 2010 census data, and key informant interviews)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Resumen/Abstract; PDF pp. 2-3, Introducción
